title: Lumen Saga: a browser MMORPG built by one person plus several AI coding agents. Open Beta is live
author: gunnrcrakr
selftext:
Hi r/aigamedev! I've been building **Lumen Saga**, a browser MMORPG (Thai + English) that's now in Open Beta with real players. I wanted to share how it's made, because most of the day-to-day work is done by AI agents.

**How the "team" works**

* Several AI coding agents work in parallel, each in its own local worktree. To avoid collisions they claim a version number before they touch main.
* Every change gets a version bump, a regression test and a bilingual patch note. The game is on v0.25.1527 now.
* The rule I learned the hard way: agents never deploy on their own. They build, test and show me screenshots, and I say "push" or "deploy".
* Another agent turns the patch notes into posts for our Facebook Page, and a dev agent fact-checks every number against the game code before anything goes out.

**What's in the game**

* A hero team with a skill-gem system: active gems, support gems that change how a skill behaves, and companion and turret summons.
* The Lumen Tree for passive builds, gear with random affixes, enhancement from +1 to +15, and a player market.
* PvP that uses the same rules as PvE with a single global damage scale, so builds don't need a separate PvP version.
* Seasons: Season 0 is running now.

**Lessons so far**

* AI is great at shipping lots of small changes, but you need tests that lock in past decisions, or old bugs come back.
* Write every design decision down. Agents don't remember last week, but the repo does.
* Balance still needs a human. I make every stat call myself.

🎮 Play free in your browser: [lumen-saga.com](https://lumen-saga.com/)  
Happy to answer anything about the workflow, the prompts or the pipeline!

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
Why is *everyone* vibe-coding MMORPGs? It's one of the trickiest, highest upkeep, complex genres out there. 95% of them are going to be shut down in a year after there ends up being no player base and the creator doesn't want to continue paying for servers.

Also, obligatory "if you can't take the time to use human words when advertising your product, why should I take the time to try it and give feedback?"
